sections.name: Reveal
sections.title: Reveal on scroll
sections.what: Watches the element and adds the marker class when enough of it is visible, then stops watching. A delay, if given, becomes a transition delay.
sections.why: Watching once, instead of all the time, saves work and stops content from hiding again.
sections.watch_out: The marker is added directly to the element. If a parent later changes the class name, React may overwrite the marker and hide the content again.

summary: A wrapper that fades and lifts its contents the first time they scroll into view.
purpose: Adds gentle entrance motion to sections without repeating the same code everywhere.
why: Likely reason: adds motion while keeping the page readable. The motion itself is defined in CSS, as the file comment says.
how: Watches its element. When at least 12 percent of it is visible, it adds a marker class and stops watching. An optional delay sets a transition delay.
inputs: The element type to use, a class name, a delay in milliseconds, and the content.
outputs: The same content, marked as revealed after it scrolls into view.
risks: Likely: the CSS starts the content hidden, so content whose observer never fires would stay hidden. The code offers no fallback.
debug: If content is missing, check whether it carries the reveal class and whether it later gets the in-view marker class.
